# Create E5 Swarm gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E5 Swarm enemy — the fast-moving, unpredictable cluster attacker from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its small, diamond-shaped neon entities moving in tight, fast clusters with sudden direction changes. This is the highest-threat regular enemy by positional threat in dense formations.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Swarm's fast, chaotic cluster movement in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of swarm/clustering movement patterns.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see Swarm enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly so I can verify the cluster movement logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Swarm enemy and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Swarm's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both cluster-only and shooting modes independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts`) renders Swarm enemies in tight, fast-moving clusters.
- [ ] **AC2 — Swarm visual style:** Swarms render as small, diamond-shaped neon entities (blue `#0066ff` per GDD §4.1) in groups, consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Cluster movement:** Enemies move in tight, fast-moving clusters that change direction suddenly. Clusters stay together but can split and rejoin.
- [ ] **AC4 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Swarm enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC5 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Swarms fire coordinated burst shots (simulating Level 4 behaviour). When off, Swarms only cluster. When on, they fire coordinated bursts.
- [ ] **AC6 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Swarms pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD, no power-ups.
- **Enemy behaviour:** Swarms are 1 HP, destroyed by a single bullet. No health bar needed.
- **Cluster dynamics:** Swarms should feel fast and unpredictable. Clusters of 3–5 enemies move together, can split and rejoin.
- **Firing:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Swarms fire coordinated bursts (multiple enemies firing simultaneously in the same direction).
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, fast movement whoosh, and destruction (sharp, quick sound).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` — The Swarm gym scene.
- `src/entities/Swarm.ts` — Swarm enemy entity (cluster movement + coordinated firing logic).
- `src/assets/` — Swarm sprite (blue diamond shape).
- `src/audio/` — Swarm-related sound effects (spawn, movement, destruction).

## Related work

- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** — related; implements V-formation pattern.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; will refactor code across enemy gym scenes.
- **Gym index scene (AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ)** — related; will link to this scene from the gym index.
- **Game Design Document (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec, §4.1 E5 Swarm definition.

## Best practices (mandatory — see docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md)

This scene MUST be built on the shared core gym formation-scene library and follow the conventions documented in **`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`** (see §3 "Best practice: adding a new enemy gym scene" and §5 "Extending the core library"). In particular:

- Extend `GymFormationScene` (src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts) wherever the scene is a formation-driven gym scene; supply only entity-specific configuration (`EnemyFormationConfig`), constants, and thin test accessors — DO NOT copy the ~200-line formation/UI/bullet boilerplate from the pre-refactor `GymScout`/`GymDiver`/`GymTank`.
- Movement that exceeds `applyFormationPosition()`'s flat-translation contract (e.g. E4 orbital paths, E5 clusters, Boss phases) belongs in the **entity** or as a new seam in the core library per §5 — never by duplicating scene boilerplate.
- Reuse the shared formation-offset builders in `src/utils/formations.ts` for any grid/formation geometry; add new pure builders there with unit tests.
- Follow the new-scene checklist: `add.existing()` for display-list membership, `lineStyle()` after `clear()` in entity drawing, exported tuning constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests (spawn count, geometry, drift, EXPLODE, SHOOT toggle, `← INDEX`).
- Update `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1/§3 if this scene introduces a new convention.

- [ ] **AC9 — Core library reuse:** The scene extends the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (or an approved core-library seam per §5 of `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) and contains no duplicated formation/UI/bullet boilerplate.
- [ ] **AC10 — Guide compliance:** The implementation follows the new-scene checklist in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§3): `add.existing()`, `lineStyle()` after `clear()`, exported constants, test accessors, and per-scene tests.

# Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the Boss — "The Central AI" from GDD §4.3. The scene should show its multi-phase health bar, 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases, and complex bullet patterns. This is the final challenge enemy with unique mechanics (multi-hit health, phase transitions).

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing boss behaviour — wants to see all boss attack phases, health bar, and bullet patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of multi-phase boss behaviour with health bar management.

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Boss cycle through 3–4 distinct attack pattern phases so I can verify the phase transition logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to see a 4-phase health bar that visually depletes as the Boss takes damage so I can verify the health bar rendering.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to deal damage to the Boss so I can test health bar progression and phase transitions.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear visual and audio cues before each boss attack phase begins so I can verify the telegraphing system.

- [ ] **AC4 — Boss attack phases implemented:** All Boss phases from the GDD are present:
  - **Phase 1:** Spread — Boss fires bullets in a wide spread pattern.
  - **Phase 2:** Spiral — Bullets spiral outward from the Boss in a rotating pattern.
  - **Phase 3:** Pulse — Screen-wide pulse wave expands from the Boss, followed by aimed shots at the player's last known position.
  - **Phase 4 — Desperation:** All previous patterns combined at higher speed; Boss core becomes more exposed/bright (visual cue).
- [ ] **AC5 — Damage button:** A button on-screen deals damage to the Boss, advancing the health bar through phases. Visual cues (core exposure) change at each phase transition.
- [ ] **AC6 — Telegraphing:** Each attack phase begins with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the visual event.

- **Enemy behaviour:** The Boss is multi-hit (4 phases). Each phase has a distinct visual representation and attack pattern.
- **Phase transitions:** Visual cues (core exposure, brightness) indicate phase progression. Audio cues announce transitions.
- **Firing:** All Boss attack phases fire complex bullet patterns. Patterns should be learnable but increasingly difficult as phases progress.
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, each phase's unique audio cue, phase transitions, and destruction.

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — Boss enemy entity (multi-phase health + attack patterns).

# Create gym scene for non-combat power-ups (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet) with round-robin spawning, collection, and standalone power-up HUD

## Problem statement

The gym suite (GymIndex + per-mechanic scenes) currently has no scene demonstrating power-up spawning, collection, and HUD feedback: the existing gym scenes explicitly exclude HUD and power-ups. This item adds a single `GymPowerUps` scene (auto-discovered by the gym index) that cycles through the **non-weapon, non-combat** power-ups **P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet** round-robin — each spawns every 5 s, grows from nothing to full size, sits stationary for 5 s, shrinks to nothing and despawns — while the player ship flies around collecting them. Collected power-ups apply their **full behaviour** (observable without threats) and their states (timers, stack counts, lives) are rendered by a **standalone HUD class** designed to be attachable to any Phaser scene.

> **Scope boundary (per operator, three-way split):**
> - **Weapon power-ups** (P1 Spread Shot, P2 Rapid Fire + new weapon patterns) → sibling **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** ("Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene", in-progress).
> - **Combat-coupled power-ups** (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport — full behaviour demonstrable only with threats) → sibling **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** ("Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups… with low-level enemy threats").
> - **This item = non-combat, threat-free gym: P5, P8, P9**, plus the shared spawn/lifecycle mechanics, ship, and the standalone HUD class (the combat scene depends on this item for those reusable pieces).

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each non-combat power-up spawn, grow, sit, shrink, and fade in isolation, and to verify collection + effect application + HUD feedback feel right before any combat is added.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a reusable power-up lifecycle (spawn/grow/hold/shrink/collect), per-type effect behaviour, and a standalone HUD that any future scene (main game, other gyms, the combat gym) can attach.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to fly over a grown power-up to collect it, so I can see its effect take hold (e.g., a faster ship, a lives bump, drops drifting toward me) and watch it appear on the HUD.
- As a **player**, I want the HUD to show the active power-ups with remaining timers (timed types) and counts (stackable/permanent types), so I always know what is currently active.
- As a **developer**, I want re-collecting a timed power-up to refresh its timer to the full duration, so repeated pickups behave predictably.
- As a **developer**, I want the HUD to be a standalone class any scene can instantiate, so the main game and the combat gym don't have to re-implement power-up status UI.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single gym scene with ship:** A new `GymPowerUps` scene (key `GymPowerUps`, label `PowerUps`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with the standard thrust movement + screen-wrap from `GymPlayer`, and has the shared "← INDEX" back button.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the non-combat power-ups **P5, P8, P9 in ascending GDD order (P5 Speed Boost, P8 Extra Life, P9 Magnet)**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime. On spawn the drop **grows from scale 0 to full size**; on despawn it **shrinks to nothing** then is removed; growth/shrink are delta-time driven (framerate-independent) and the window durations are tunable constants.
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (i.e., during grow, full-size hold, and shrink until it drops below the threshold); collecting requires the ship to overlap the drop. A drop that fades uncollected is removed with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — Full per-type behaviour (threat-free):** Collecting each type applies its full GDD §4.4 behaviour as observable without threats: **P5 Speed Boost** — +50% movement speed (thrust/max-speed) applied live to the ship's movement for 10 s; **P8 Extra Life** — +1 life immediately (cap 5, excess ignored), reflected in the HUD lives counter (starting at 3); **P9 Magnet** — permanent effect, one stack per pickup (cap 5), radius 2× ship size +50% per stack, attracting on-screen power-up drops toward the ship at a speed slower than the ship's max speed.
- [ ] **AC5 — Timer refresh:** Re-collecting an already-active timed power-up (P5) refreshes its timer to the full duration (not additive, not ignored). Permanent/passive types follow their own rules (P9 stacks to cap 5 then no-op; P8 excess ignored above cap 5).
- [ ] **AC6 — Standalone HUD class:** A standalone `src/ui/HUD.ts` class (Phaser game-object based, attachable to any scene, rendered above gameplay) shows, for each active power-up: **icon, name, and either a remaining-seconds timer (timed types) or a stack/pickup count (P9 magnet stacks)**, plus the **lives count** (P8). The gym scene uses this HUD; the class contains no gym-specific logic and is reusable by the combat gym scene (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: spawn timing + round-robin order, grow/shrink lifecycle, the 3% collection threshold, effect timers + refresh semantics, P8 cap, P9 stacking cap + attraction math, and the HUD's model (timer/count/lives aggregation, scene-attachability). Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, collection, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains the `GymPowerUps` scene and `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel entries).
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons are code-drawn per GDD §4.4 icon suggestions.
- **Scope:** this gym is threat-free (no enemies, no enemy bullets). Weapon power-ups (P1/P2 + new weapon patterns) belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; combat-coupled types (P3/P4/P6/P7) belong to AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40.
- **Spawn cadence:** one spawn every 5 s; 5 s lifetime → exactly one drop on screen at any time (spawn of the next coincides with despawn of the previous), round-robin over P5 → P8 → P9 then repeat.
- **HUD reusability:** the HUD must be a standalone class attachable to any scene — it must not import or depend on gym-only code (the combat gym depends on it).
- **Collection geometry:** overlap-based (drop radius + ship hull radius), gated by the 3% scale threshold.
- **Growth/shrink windows:** default 0.5 s grow / 0.5 s shrink inside the 5 s lifetime (tunable constants in `src/core/constants.ts`), leaving ~4 s at full size.
- **Re-collection:** timed effects refresh to full duration (operator decision Q5; captured in AC5).

## Existing state

- Gym infrastructure exists: `GymIndex` (auto-discovery via `import.meta.glob` on `src/scenes/gym/*.ts`, labels, "← INDEX" nav via `src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`), base formation scene (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`), and scenes `GymPlayer`, `GymScout`, `GymDiver`, `GymTank` — all explicitly "no HUD, no power-ups".
- Player ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`) with live-tunable config (`src/core/config.ts`).
- **No power-up or HUD code exists** in `src/` (no `powerups/` nor `ui/HUD.ts` yet). GDD §4.4 defines P1–P9 semantics and icon suggestions; GDD §6.4 architecture plans `powerups/` and `ui/HUD.ts`.
- Sibling AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR (in-progress) covers weapon power-ups with its own weapon gym scene, using the same spawn/grow/shrink/3%-collection mechanics (7 s lifetime there).
- Sibling AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40 (new, depends on this item) covers the combat-coupled power-ups P3/P4/P6/P7 in a combat gym scene with E1 Scout threats.
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom; `Scout` entity (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) provides `tryFireAimedBullet`, formation offsets and destroy lifecycle for the sibling combat scene.

## Desired change

1. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — single scene: ship (reused `Player` + movement), round-robin power-up spawner (P5 → P8 → P9, one per 5 s), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, overlap collection gated at scale > 3%, per-type effect application (P5/P8/P9), HUD attachment, back button.
2. Add a power-up implementation under `src/powerups/` (base lifecycle class + type catalogue for the non-combat types; icon drawing) — following the GDD §6.4 layout (`PowerUp.ts` base etc.), kept in a form reusable by the main game and the combat gym, which extends the catalogue with P3/P4/P6/P7 entries and threat-coupled effect hooks.
3. Add `src/ui/HUD.ts` — standalone class attachable to any scene, rendering above gameplay (Phaser Container + text): active power-up icons, names, timers/counts, and lives.
4. Add constants for the spawn/lifecycle tuning to `src/core/constants.ts`.
5. Update the GDD §6.4 architecture briefly (list `GymPowerUps`; note `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel as implemented).
6. Tests: unit tests for lifecycle/timing/round-robin/threshold/effects/magnet/HUD model + scene tests via gameHarness.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — **new** gym scene (the deliverable).
- `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` — **new** base power-up class (spawn/grow/hold/shrink/collect lifecycle).
- `src/powerups/types.ts` (or `PowerUpTypes.ts`) — **new** power-up catalogue (P5/P8/P9 entries here; P3/P4/P6/P7 entries added by the combat-gym item): id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics per GDD §4.4.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — **new** active-effects registry: timers, lives, live movement multiplier (P5), magnet attractor (P9).
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — **new** code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 suggestions (used by both field drops and HUD).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **new** standalone HUD class (attachable to any scene; icons/timers/counts/lives).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — spawn interval, lifetime, grow/shrink windows, collection threshold (3%), sizing constants.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.test.ts` (+ power-up/effect/HUD unit tests) — **new** tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §6.4 architecture: add `GymPowerUps`, note `ui/HUD.ts` power-up panel implemented.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** — "Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups… with low-level enemy threats": sibling that **depends on this item** (reuses the power-up lifecycle + catalogue + HUD) and adds the combat-coupled types P3/P4/P6/P7 with E1 Scout threats. Dependency edge: combat-gym → this item.
- **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** — "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene" (in-progress): sibling gym for weapon power-ups; same round-robin/grow/shrink/3%-collection mechanics with a 7 s lifetime; sets the scope boundary (weapon types excluded here). Related-to (shared lifecycle mechanics, complementary scope) — should not drift apart.
- **GymPlayer scene** — ship movement/input pattern reused by this scene.
- **"Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — the player gym; precedent for `Player` reuse.
- **"Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes" (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK) + core library (AH-0MTAN4IFR007U9B3)** — the shared gym base-class pattern (buttons, back button, discovery exclusions) this scene should follow.
- GDD power-up catalog items (completed): "Add an extra life power up" (AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3), "Add a Magnet power up" (AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V) — semantics source for P8/P9.
- GDD items (completed): "Game Design Document for AI_Hell" (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — non-combat split:** combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) were removed from this item per operator direction (see Appendix Q7/Q8); this item covers P5/P8/P9 only and provides the shared lifecycle/HUD the combat scene depends on.
- **Assumption — P8 lives counter:** the HUD lives counter starts at 3 and increments on P8 collection (cap 5) exactly as the GDD lives model; no hits occur in this threat-free gym, so lives are never lost here.
- **Assumption — growth/shrink windows:** 0.5 s grow / 0.5 s shrink (tunable) inside the 5 s lifetime; collection allowed whenever scale > 3% (roughly the whole window except the first/last moments).
- **Assumption — icons:** code-drawn neon icons per GDD §4.4 suggestions, consistent with the code-first/no-asset convention; shared between field drops and HUD.
- **Scope-creep guard:** weapon power-ups, combat-coupled power-ups, enemy/bullet threat sources, score display, main-menu HUD variants, and gameplay-scene integration are out of scope; record any extras as linked work items.
- **Risk — sibling divergence:** both sibling gyms (weapon AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR, combat AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40) use the same spawn cadence/3% mechanics; if they land first with different constants or a shared lifecycle module, coordinate to avoid divergent implementations (extract a shared lifecycle util if needed).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 (round 1): "Should there be a single `GymPowerUps` scene that cycles through all power-up types, or separate gym scenes per type?" — Answer (operator): **"1. single"** — one scene cycles all types round-robin. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 (round 1): "Which power-up types should the gym cover — all 9 or a subset?" — Answer (operator): **"2. all of them"** — subsequently split three ways (see Q4/Q6/Q7): weapons → AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; combat-coupled → AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40; here = P5/P8/P9. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 (round 1): "For the standalone HUD, what should it display and should it be a Phaser scene or DOM overlay?" — Answer (operator): **"Active effect timers, collection counts as applicable for stackable items, icons. Your call re phaser scene vs overlay as long as it can be displayed over another schene [scene]."** — Research: no HUD code exists; `GymPlayer` uses a DOM overlay, gym scenes use Phaser text/graphics; a Phaser game-object class attachable to any scene (Container above gameplay) fits the neon aesthetic and the existing harness. Decision: standalone `src/ui/HUD.ts` class, Phaser-side, attachable to any scene.
- Q4 (round 2): "Combat-only power-ups (P1/P2/P4/P6/P7) — implement full behaviour in the gym or register-only timers?" — Answer (operator): **"Do not include weapon power ups in this gym scene (there is another work item for those), any powerups that are present in this scene should implement full behaviour."** — Research: `wl search weapon` found **AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR** (in-progress "Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene"). Final accepted: weapon power-ups excluded (sibling item); all power-ups present here implement full behaviour.
- Q5 (round 2): "Re-collecting an already-active timed power-up — reset timer to full duration (refresh) or ignore?" — Answer (operator): **"2. refresh"** — timer refreshes to full duration. Source: interactive reply.
- Q6 (round 3): "Shield/Bomb/PhaseShift/Teleport full behaviour needs threats to demonstrate. Add a minimal threat source (e.g., bullet-spawn button) or keep the gym threat-free?" — Answer (operator): **"There are no threats. There is another work item to create a gym for other power ups."** — Final accepted (round 4, scope split): the combat-coupled power-ups (P3/P4/P6/P7) were pulled out of this item into the new combat gym scene item AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40; threat sources live there. This item keeps the threat-free types P5/P8/P9. Second answer (this round): **"Just use scout (with shooting)"** — the combat scene's threat is an E1 Scout formation with shooting enabled. Sources: interactive replies.

# Weapon power-ups (3 patterns + reset) with auto-fire and weapon gym scene

## Problem statement

The player ship currently has **no firing capability at all** — the GDD (§2.3) promises auto-fire, but the `Player` entity only renders and moves. This item gives the ship its first real weapon: a default single-shot **cannon** firing in the direction of travel, plus **three weapon power-ups** (Spread, Dual, Rapid) that swap the equipped weapon **persistently** (no timer — active until another weapon power-up is collected), and a **fourth power-up** that returns the ship to the starting cannon. A new `GymWeapons` scene demonstrates spawning, collection, and the shot patterns round-robin.

> **Deviation from GDD:** GDD §4.4 P1/P2 ("Spread Shot", "Rapid Fire") are *timed* (10 s). Per operator, weapon power-ups here are **persistent until replaced** — the GDD's weapon semantics need a documentation update to match (in scope as documentation).

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each weapon's shot pattern in isolation, collect the power-ups, and verify that weapon switching is instant, persistent, and that the Reset power-up returns to the starting cannon.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a reusable weapon catalogue (pattern + fire rate + bullet visuals per weapon), a heading-based fire direction model, and shared power-up spawn/lifecycle timing reusable by the sibling power-up gyms.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to fly over a grown weapon power-up to collect it, so my ship immediately starts firing that weapon's pattern in my direction of travel.
- As a **player**, I want my collected weapon to stay active until I collect a different one, so there are no surprise "power-downs" mid-run.
- As a **player**, I want angled pattern shots (e.g. Spread, or a hypothetical 180° shot) to be relative to my direction of travel, so if I'm travelling right (90°) a backward shot flies at 270°.
- As a **developer**, I want spawn/lifetime/grow/shrink timings shared and parameterised between the weapon gym (7 s) and the non-weapon power-up gym (5 s), so cadence differences are configuration, not duplicated code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Auto-fire weapon system:** The player ship auto-fires its equipped weapon in the direction of movement (current velocity heading; most-recent heading when stationary) with no fire button (GDD §2.3). Four weapon definitions exist — **Cannon** (single bullet), **Spread** (3-bullet fan: -30°/0°/+30° relative to heading), **Dual** (2 parallel bullets offset perpendicular to heading), **Rapid** (single bullets at a markedly higher rate) — each with its own fire rate and distinct bullet appearance, as tunable constants.
- [ ] **AC2 — Persistent switching + reset:** Collecting a weapon power-up instantly equips its weapon. The equipped weapon persists **with no timer** until another weapon power-up is collected. Collecting the **Reset** power-up returns the ship to the starting **Cannon**.
- [ ] **AC3 — GymWeapons scene + round-robin lifecycle:** A new `GymWeapons` scene (auto-discovered by the gym index, key `GymWeapons`, label `Weapons`) renders the ship (thrust movement + screen-wrap, "← INDEX" back button) and spawns the drops **Spread → Dual → Rapid → Reset** round-robin, one at a time, stationary at a fixed position. Each drop is on screen for **7 seconds** (tunable), growing from scale 0 to full size on spawn and shrinking to nothing on despawn (delta-time driven, framerate-independent), and is removed after its lifetime if uncollected.
- [ ] **AC4 — Collection gating:** A drop is collectible once its current scale is **≥ 3% of full size** (during grow, hold, and shrink while above threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop (drop radius + ship hull radius). Collecting a drop plays the pickup cue and applies its weapon effect; collecting does not pause or reset the next spawn's cadence.
- [ ] **AC5 — Shared timing infrastructure:** The spawn/lifetime/grow/shrink timing used by this scene is implemented in **shared, parameterised code** (extracted during this implementation so it is reusable by the sibling power-up gym AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT): weapon drops use the 7 s lifetime, non-weapon drops use 5 s, via configuration — no duplicated spawn code.
- [ ] **AC6 — Distinctive visuals + audio:** Each power-up is visually distinctive (code-drawn neon, matching the project's no-asset art style) and its shape visually hints at its shot pattern (fan arc for Spread, parallel bars for Dual, waveform for Rapid, return/undo arrow for Reset). Audio cues play on **spawn, despawn, and collection** (Web Audio synthesis via `src/audio/effects.ts`, safe no-op fallback as today).
- [ ] **AC7 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: pattern direction math (e.g. a 180° backward shot with heading 90° → absolute 270°), heading-from-velocity with most-recent-heading fallback when stationary, per-weapon fire rates, round-robin order, grow/shrink lifecycle, the ≥ 3% collection threshold, persistent (un-timed) switching, and Reset returning to Cannon. Scene tests (gameHarness) verify auto-discovery, ship presence, auto-fire producing bullets, and collection swapping the weapon. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, the GDD (§2.3 auto-fire and §4.4 weapon power-up semantics — persistent vs timed), the gym index scene list, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- [ ] **AC9 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — no external art assets; bullets are drawn graphics like the existing `ScoutBullet` (no physics bodies).
- **Threat-free gym:** no enemies, no enemy bullets, no collision damage — player bullets are demonstration-only: they fly in their pattern and are removed off-screen. (Combat-coupled demonstration belongs to sibling AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40.)
- **Out of scope (per operator):** the power-up status **HUD** (tracked in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) and non-weapon/non-combat power-up behaviours (P5/P8/P9 in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) and combat-coupled behaviours (P3/P4/P6/P7 in AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40).
- **Dependency floor:** this item **depends on** AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT (dependency edge added) — the shared power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics are expected to exist or be extractable when this is implemented; this item's implementation extracts the shared, parameterised timing library.
- **Firing direction:** from the current velocity vector (atan2); when speed ≈ 0, fire along the **most recent** non-zero heading; angled shots are offsets relative to that heading (a 0° offset fires straight along travel). Default heading before any movement is configurable (e.g. 0° = right).
- **Spawn cadence (assumption):** one drop on screen at a time; the next drop spawns as the previous despawns (7 s cadence, consistent with the sibling 5 s cadence). Tunable.
- **Fire-rate defaults (assumption, tunable constants):** Cannon ≈ 400 ms, Spread ≈ 600 ms, Dual ≈ 500 ms, Rapid ≈ 125 ms; bullet speed ≈ 350 px/s; grow-in ≈ 0.5 s, shrink-out ≈ 0.5 s inside the 7 s lifetime (~6 s at full size).

## Existing state

- `Player` entity (`src/entities/Player.ts`) renders + moves (thrust/flame); **no weapon, firing, or bullet code exists** anywhere in `src/` for the player.
- Movement model (`src/utils/movement.ts`) exposes `vx`/`vy` in the movement state — the heading source. `Player` keeps `_movementState` privately; a heading accessor or velocity getter is needed.
- Bullet precedent: `ScoutBullet` (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) — a Graphics-based bullet with `vx`/`vy`, advanced by the scene and removed off-screen. The formation gym scenes (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`) own bullet lifecycles.
- Gym infrastructure: auto-discovery via `import.meta.glob` on `src/scenes/gym/*.ts` (no registry edits needed for a new scene), `addBackToIndexButton` (`src/utils/gymNavigation.ts`), gameHarness tests (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`).
- Audio: `src/audio/effects.ts` has synthetic spawn/destruction cues and a safe no-op fallback; pickup/spawn-despawn/weapon-change cues will be added here.
- Sibling power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (depends-on, currently intake-complete) delivers the generic power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics + standalone HUD; **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** (sibling, combat-coupled) also depends on it.
- GDD §2.3 specifies auto-fire; §4.4 P1 (Spread Shot, 3-bullet fan) and P2 (Rapid Fire) are currently timed (10 s) — reconciled to persistent semantics by this item (documentation update).

## Desired change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable **weapon catalogue + heading math** module (e.g. `src/utils/weapons.ts`): per-weapon definitions (name, pattern offsets, fire rate, bullet colour/shape), `absoluteAngle = heading + offset`, and bullet creation data from a heading.
2. Extend the **Player** entity: expose heading (velocity-derived, most-recent fallback), an equipped-weapon slot with `equipWeapon(id)`/`resetWeapon()`, a fire cooldown, and auto-fire emission suitable for the scene to spawn bullets.
3. Add a **player bullet** (Graphics-drawn, `vx`/`vy`, removed off-screen) + scene-owned bullet lifecycle in the gym scene (patterned on the enemy gym bullets).
4. Add **weapon power-up drops** (Spread, Dual, Rapid, Reset): code-drawn distinctive shapes, grown/shrunk by scale, collectible ≥ 3%, applying weapon equip/reset on collection, leveraging the shared spawn mechanics from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT, extracting the shared parameterised timing.
5. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — ship + auto-fire + round-robin spawner (7 s) + collection + back button; auto-discovered by the index.
6. Add audio cues (spawn/despawn/pickup/weapon-change) to `src/audio/effects.ts`.
7. Tests (unit + scene harness) and documentation (GDD, README, code comments).

## Key Files

- `src/utils/weapons.ts` — NEW — pure weapon catalogue (patterns, rates, bullet visuals) + heading-relative angle math.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — add heading, weapon slot (`equipWeapon`/`resetWeapon`), fire cooldown + auto-fire emission.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts` — NEW — Graphics bullet (circle) with `vx`/`vy`, off-screen removal.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — NEW — auto-fired ship + round-robin weapon-drop spawner (7 s) + collection + back button.
- `src/powerups/…` / shared timing — reuse/extract shared spawn/lifecycle code from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with parameterised lifetime (7 s here / 5 s there).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add spawn/despawn/pickup/weapon-change cues.
- `src/core/constants.ts` (or a new weapon-config module) — tunable lifetimes, fire rates, grow/shrink windows, scale threshold.

## Risks & assumptions

- **GDD semantics deviation (timed → persistent weapons):** the GDD currently defines P1/P2 as timed (10 s) effects; this item makes weapon power-ups persistent until replaced. Mitigated by the documentation AC (AC8) — a GDD update explicitly reconciling §4.4 weapon semantics.
- **Scope of "implied" work:** the player ship has zero firing code today; the baseline auto-fire + cannon + weapon-switch machinery is the bulk of the work, not the power-ups themselves. Plan accordingly (this is a feature, not a tweak).
- **Sibling dependency (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT):** shared spawn/lifecycle mechanics may not exist yet when implementation starts; the design assumes the shared parameterised timing is extractable from (or contributed back to) the sibling. The dependency edge + explicit extraction AC (AC5) keep this honest — surface a blocker work item if the sibling's shared code is unusable.
- **Scope-creep risk:** HUD, non-combat (P5/P8/P9) and combat-coupled (P3/P4/P6/P7) power-up behaviours are deliberately out of scope and live in sibling items (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT, AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40). Any new power-up/mechanic discovered during implementation should be recorded as a linked work item, not folded into this one.
- **Direction edge cases:** firing when stationary (use most-recent heading), and before any movement (configurable default heading, e.g. 0° = right) — covered by pure heading math + unit tests (AC7).
- **No physics bodies:** bullets and collection use distance/overlap checks on Graphics (project precedent), not Phaser Arcade bodies; keep it that way for consistency.

## Related work

- **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (this item **depends on**): "Create gym scene for power-ups with spawning, collection, and standalone HUD" — generic power-up spawn/lifecycle mechanics (5 s cadence) + standalone HUD; source of the shared timing to extract/parameterise.
- **AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40** (sibling): "Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups…" — also depends on AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT; shares the extracted spawn library.
- **AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S** (completed): "Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" — `GymPlayer` + `Player` foundation.
- **GDD (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)**: §2.3 auto-fire, §4.4 power-ups (P1/P2 timed semantics to be reconciled).
- **AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1** (completed): "Bring simple audio effects into MVP scope in GDD" — §7.3 audio design this implementation follows.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The three additional shot patterns — what should they be? (suggestions: spread/fan, dual side-by-side, rapid-fire burst, or something else?)" — Answer (rgardler, interactive): "as you suggest" → **Spread (3-bullet fan), Dual (2 side-by-side), Rapid (burst)**.
- Q2: "Firing mechanism — auto-fire or fire button?" — Answer: **auto-fire** (matches GDD §2.3).
- Q3: "Direction of shots — all patterns fire in direction of travel?" — Answer: **yes, direction of movement (or most recent movement)**; angled shots are relative to that direction — "if a power up fires a shot backwards (180 degrees) and the ship is travelling to the right (90°) the shot will be at 270°".
- Q4: "Visual design for power-ups?" — Answer: operator delegated — **make them very distinctive from one another, each providing a visual clue to its shot pattern** (fan arc, parallel bars, waveform, undo/return arrow).
- Q5: "Audio — collection sound? spawn/despawn cues?" — Answer: **yes and yes**.
- Q6: "Shooting rate — one rate or per-weapon?" — Answer: **each weapon has its own fire rate**.
- Q7: "Relationship to existing power-up gym item AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT?" — Answer: **separate items** — the existing one covers non-combat power-ups (P5/P8/P9); a third intake (AH-0MTC2P6G3007PJ40) covers combat-coupled ones; this covers weapon power-ups. All three separate but related.
- Q8: "7 s vs 5 s on-screen?" — Answer: **7 s for weapons, 5 s for others** — shared code manages the difference; this item **depends on** AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT and **extracts the shared library** when implementing.
- Q9: "HUD scope?" — Answer: **out of scope** for this item (tracked in AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).

> Prior answers changed: none — all answers above are the final accepted versions.

# Create combat gym scene for combat-coupled power-ups (P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport) with low-level enemy threats

## Problem statement

Four power-up types in the GDD catalogue — **P3 Shield, P4 Bomb, P6 Phase Shift, P7 Teleport** — cannot demonstrate their full behaviour without threats: Shield must absorb a hit, Bomb must clear on-screen enemy bullets, Phase Shift must pass through enemies and bullets, and Teleport must search for a safe spot free of threats. The operator split these "combat-coupled" types out of the threat-free power-up gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT) into this dedicated **combat gym scene** that contains a **low-level enemy threat (E1 Scout with shooting)**. The scene shares the round-robin spawn lifecycle, grow-shrink animation, 3% collection threshold, player ship, and standalone HUD class with the non-combat gym, on which this item depends.

## Users

- **Player / developer testing the game** — wants to see each combat-coupled power-up's full effect against real (but low-level) threats: a shield bubble popping on a hit, a bomb wiping a bullet cloud, ghosting straight through a formation, and blinking away to a safe spot.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need the threat-coupled behaviour (hit absorption, bullet clearing, intangibility, safe-spot resolution) implemented and tested once, in a form the main game can reuse.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want my shield bubble to absorb exactly one hit and pop, so I can verify the GDD's "absorbs one hit" rule.
- As a **player**, I want to collect a Bomb while scouts are firing and see every on-screen enemy bullet vanish, with enemies untouched (they are 1 HP, GDD §4.4).
- As a **player**, I want Phase Shift to let me fly straight through the scout formation and its bullets without being hit, for 3 seconds.
- As a **player**, I want to press Space with a collected Teleport to jump to the nearest safe spot (free of scouts and bullets) along my travel direction, gaining Phase Shift on arrival.
- As a **developer**, I want the ship's hit response (no shield/phase shift) to be a simple flash/reset with no lives counter, so the demo keeps a pure combat focus.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Combat scene with ship + low-level threats:** A new `GymPowerUpsCombat` scene (key `GymPowerUpsCombat`, label `PowerUps Combat`) is defined in `src/scenes/gym/`, auto-discovered and listed by the gym index, boots correctly, renders the player ship with standard thrust movement + screen-wrap, and contains a **formation of E1 Scout enemies** (reusing `src/entities/Scout.ts` + the formation utilities) with a **SHOOT toggle** that enables aimed enemy fire at the **ship's live position** (not the fixed demo target), so hits are demonstrable. Shared "← INDEX" back button present.
- [ ] **AC2 — Round-robin spawn/lifecycle:** The scene spawns exactly the combat-coupled power-ups **P3, P4, P6, P7 in ascending GDD order**, one every 5 s, each remaining stationary for a 5 s lifetime; spawn = **grow from scale 0 to full size**, despawn = **shrink to nothing**; growth/shrink delta-time driven with the same tunable constants as the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT).
- [ ] **AC3 — Collection rule:** A drop is collectible only while its current scale is **> 3% of full size** (grow, hold, and shrink until below threshold); collection requires the ship to overlap the drop; an uncollected drop fades with no effect.
- [ ] **AC4 — P3 Shield full behaviour:** Collecting P3 arms a shield bubble rendered around the ship for **15 s**; the bubble **absorbs exactly one hit** (enemy body or enemy bullet) and then pops (effect ends, no ship flash/reset for that hit); if never hit, it expires after 15 s. Re-collection while active refreshes the timer to 15 s.
- [ ] **AC5 — P4 Bomb full behaviour:** Collecting P4 instantly removes **all on-screen enemy bullets** (aimed scout fire in-flight), does **not damage enemies** (GDD §4.4 note), is not a timed effect, and shows a brief HUD notice. Re-collection while enemies are not firing is a benign no-op (bullets cleared anyway).
- [ ] **AC6 — P6 Phase Shift full behaviour:** Collecting P6 renders a ghost-outline ship for **3 s** during which the ship **passes through enemy bodies and enemy bullets without being hit**; hit checks are disabled for the duration. Re-collection refreshes the timer to 3 s.
- [ ] **AC7 — P7 Teleport full behaviour:** P7 **stacks FIFO** (each pickup = one use); pressing **Space** consumes the earliest-collected use and teleports the ship **along the current travel direction to the nearest safe spot** — a position free of enemy bodies and enemy bullets in a safety radius, clamped to screen bounds; if no safe spot exists in the travel direction, the ship teleports to the nearest on-screen safe position anyway; on arrival the ship **gains P6 Phase Shift (3 s)** per GDD. HUD shows the teleport count.
- [ ] **AC8 — Hit response (no shield/phase shift):** Being hit by an enemy body or enemy bullet with no active P3/P6 triggers a **simple flash/reset with no lives counter** (e.g., brief invulnerability + reposition), per operator decision; this is the only consequence — no lives, no game over.
- [ ] **AC9 — HUD reuse:** The scene uses the **standalone HUD class from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) unchanged for active-effect icons, names, timers (P3/P6), and counts (P7); **no lives counter** in this scene; the HUD class itself is not modified with gym/combat-specific logic (any extension lives in the scene).
- [ ] **AC10 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover: P3 absorb-then-pop on a hit + 15 s expiry + refresh; P4 clearing all bullets without enemy damage; P6 pass-through (no hits during 3 s) + refresh; P7 FIFO stack/consume, safe-spot resolution (avoiding scouts/bullets, clamped), fallback when no safe spot, and P6-on-arrival; hit-response flash/reset (no lives); round-robin order. Scene-level tests (gameHarness) verify discovery, ship presence, scout formation + SHOOT toggle, collection against live bullets, and back button. Full suite green.
- [ ] **AC11 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (GDD §6.4 architecture gains `GymPowerUpsCombat`).
- [ ] **AC12 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine/stack:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript, Vite, Vitest (locked). Neon-vector aesthetic; code-drawn graphics only — **no external art assets**; icons code-drawn per GDD §4.4 suggestions.
- **Threats:** **E1 Scout only** (operator decision) — reuse `src/entities/Scout.ts` as-is; formation via existing utilities; **shooting toggle** enabled for the demo (bullets aimed at the ship's live position). No E2/E3/E4/E5/Boss.
- **No lives model:** hit response is flash/reset only (operator decision); P8 lives is out of scope (it lives in the non-combat gym).
- **Weapon power-ups out of scope:** P1/P2/new weapon patterns belong to AH-0MTC1TEXR006I5XR; the ship's auto-fire is NOT part of this scene (Bomb does not damage enemies, so no fire needed).
- **Shared mechanics:** the spawn cadence (one per 5 s, 5 s lifetime, 0.5 s grow/shrink) and the 3% collection threshold match the non-combat gym (AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT); constants stay in `src/core/constants.ts`; the HUD class is reused unchanged (dependency on that item).
- **Hit model details:** overlap = ship hull radius + enemy/bullet radius, exactly as the GDD "enemies are the bullets" §2.4 model; shield/phase-shift suppress the hit response; teleport safe radius is a tunable constant (proposal: ~3× ship size).

## Existing state

- Non-combat power-up gym **AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT** (intake_complete, open) delivers, first: `src/powerups/PowerUp.ts` (base lifecycle), the type catalogue + icons, `src/ui/HUD.ts` (standalone), the spawn/lifecycle constants, and `GymPowerUps` — **this item depends on those reusable pieces**. This item adds the P3/P4/P6/P7 catalogue entries + threat-coupled effect hooks.
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` exists with `tryFireAimedBullet` (currently aimed at a fixed demo target), formation offsets, alive/destroy lifecycle; `GymScout` demonstrates a V-formation with EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons via the shared `GymFormationScene` core library (`src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`).
- Ship + thrust movement exist (`src/entities/Player.ts`, `src/utils/movement.ts`, `GymPlayer.ts`).
- GDD §4.4 defines P3/P4/P6/P7 semantics and icon suggestions; §4.4 notes Bomb does not damage 1-HP enemies; §2.3 lives model (out of scope here, replaced by flash/reset).
- Tests use Vitest + a gameHarness (`src/test/gameHarness.ts`) with happy-dom.

## Desired change

1. Extend the power-up catalogue from AH-0MTC0QPS60005MNT with **P3/P4/P6/P7** entries (id, name, icon, duration/stack semantics, threat-coupled effect hooks), following the same `src/powerups/` layout.
2. Add `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — ship (reused `Player` + movement), a Scout V-formation with a SHOOT toggle (bullets aimed at the ship), the shared round-robin spawner (P3 → P4 → P6 → P7), grow/hold/shrink lifecycle, 3% collection gate, threat-coupled effect application (shield absorb, bomb clear, phase shift pass-through, teleport safe-spot), flash/reset hit response, HUD attachment (reused), back button.
3. Ship-aimed fire: extend or parameterise the Scout's fire target so bullets aim at the ship's live position (implementation may pass the ship position into the scene's fire-collection path).
4. Add safe-spot resolution (enemy/bullet-aware) + teleport consumption to `src/powerups/effects.ts`; add hit-check suppression for shield/phase-shift in the scene collision pass.

# Tank has no audio (AH-0MTCNZAPS007WTQE)

**Headline:** The E3 Tank fires 10-projectile radial bursts completely silently and has no Tank-identity audio on destruction. Add a Tank-specific mechanical-whine advance cue flowing with NO gap into a heavy cannon-thump fire sound (one cue+thump pair per burst, scene-level, at the moment of firing), following the established procedural-audio pattern; destruction reuses the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene (no double-play). Update GDD §7.3 to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation, with a cross-reference to the enemy design doc, and add this item's best practices to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.

## Problem statement

Tanks (`src/entities/Tank.ts`, gym scene `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts`) fire radial bursts silently — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns 10 projectiles with no audio — and they are indistinguishable aurally from any other enemy on destruction (only the generic shared destruction sound plays; the Tank-specific `playTankDestructionSound()` in `src/audio/effects.ts` is defined but never wired up). The Tank breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be announced) and is inconsistent with its peers (Scout has a fire sound + advance cue; Swarm has a volley burst sound; Phaser has an advance cue + destruction sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a Tank fires its radial burst (a heavy, mechanical "cannon" cue) and an advance warning so the burst is telegraphed, per GDD §7.3.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Tank audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a heavy cannon thump when a tank fires its radial burst so I can react to the projectiles.
- As a player, I want a mechanical-whine advance cue before a tank fires so I can anticipate the burst, without an awkward dead gap between warning and shot.
- As a developer, I want Tank audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests and never double-plays the destruction sound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Fire sound + advance cue** — A new Tank fire sound plays exactly **once per radial burst** (not per projectile): a heavy low "cannon thump" (`playTankFireSound()`, new). Preceded by a mechanical-whine advance cue (`playTankAdvanceCue()`, new) that flows into the thump with **no gap** (whine duration still provides the ≥ 500 ms advance lead per GDD §7.3).
- **Scene-level orchestration, one cue per burst** — `GymTank` orchestrates the cue+thump pair at the point of shooting, once per burst (Swarm-style scene-level pattern: when new bullets appear in the update loop, play the pair exactly once), not per entity/projectile.
- **Destruction sound (reuse)** — Destroying a Tank plays the shared `playDestructionSound()` exactly once per destruction (already satisfied by `GymFormationScene`). The Tank must NOT add its own destruction-sound call (no double-play); the unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is left un-wired (dead code) or removed by the implementer — not used for fire.
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — GDD §7.3 updated to record that audio-character decisions are made per-enemy at implementation and to cross-reference `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`; the enemy design doc's §3.2 GymTank row changed from "none" to the new audio pattern and §7 best-practices updated with this item's guidance (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character). All related documentation (code comments, README as applicable) updated. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill owns it).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays spawn/destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — reconcile entity-level vs scene-level audio to avoid double-play.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Tank.ts` — `tryFireRadialBurst()` spawns `TANK_BURST_COUNT = 10` projectiles silently; no audio imports. Fire interval `TANK_FIRE_INTERVAL = 2400` ms; bursts are per-entity but the scene collects them.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — thin `GymFormationScene` subclass; `collectBullets` returns `tank.tryFireRadialBurst(now)`; no audio calls.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base class plays `playSpawnSound()` at spawn and `playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()` for all enemy gyms (design doc §6/§7: base-class-owned).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playTankDestructionSound()` (220→30 Hz sawtooth, 0.45 s, vol 0.2 — "heavier, lower destruction cue") is currently **dead code** (defined, never called). Has `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`, power-up/weapon cues, `playSwarmBurstSound`, `playScoutFireSound`, `playScoutAdvanceCue`; **no Tank fire sound or advance cue exists**.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymSwarm.ts` (reference pattern) — overrides `update()` to count bullets before/after and calls `playSwarmBurstSound()` exactly once when new bullets appear (coordinated volley).
- `src/entities/Scout.ts` (reference) — two-phase tell: advance cue at tell start, then a gap, then fire sound + shot. Operator explicitly wants the Tank to have NO gap (and flagged Scout for the same treatment — see related work).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.2 — table lists `GymTank` audio as "none"; §7 no-double-play rule.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §7.3 — SFX catalog: "Enemy fire (Level 4+)" = Short zap, Low-medium, Immediate; advance telegraphing requires ≥ 500 ms lead for Level 4–5 enemy fire. No per-enemy audio-character notes; no cross-reference to the enemy design doc.
- `README.md` — does not document per-enemy Tank audio (only Scout/Boss cues); leave untouched unless discovered otherwise.

## Desired change

- **New sounds** in `src/audio/effects.ts`: `playTankAdvanceCue()` (mechanical whine, ≥ 500 ms, leading straight into the shot with no gap) and `playTankFireSound()` (heavy low cannon thump), both safe no-ops without an `AudioContext`.
- **Scene orchestration** in `GymTank` (model: `GymSwarm.update()`): when the update loop detects new bullets (a burst fired), play the advance cue immediately followed by the fire thump with no gap — exactly one cue+thump pair per burst.
- **Destruction**: no entity change — reuse the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene; test asserts no double-play. The existing unused `playTankDestructionSound()` is NOT used for firing; implementer wires it or removes it as dead code (see Q2 appendix).
- **Docs**: GDD §7.3 note + cross-reference; enemy design doc §3.2 row + §7 best practices from this item.

**Key Files:**

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — add `playTankAdvanceCue()` and `playTankFireSound()` (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op guard); decide fate of dead `playTankDestructionSound()`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — override `update()` (Swarm pattern) to detect new bullets and play the cue+thump pair once per burst at the point of shooting.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.test.ts` — add spy-based tests: one cue+thump pair per burst, cue precedes thump with no gap, no double destruction sound, headless no-op degradation (see `GymSwarm.test.ts` / `GymScout.test.ts` for the established test pattern).
- `src/entities/Tank.test.ts` — only if firing-path changes require entity-level assertions; prefer scene-level tests.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — no change expected (base class already owns spawn/destruction audio).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3: per-enemy audio-character decision note + cross-reference to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §3.2 `GymTank` audio column from "none" to the new pattern; §7 best-practices additions (no-gap cue→thump for Tank, per-enemy audio character allowed).
- `README.md` — only if it documents per-enemy Tank audio (checked: it does not; leave untouched unless discovered otherwise).

## Related work

- **Swarm has no audio (AH-0MTCO1L74003CAQJ)** — in_review; the sibling item that added Swarm audio (scene-level volley burst sound, no advance cue) — the orchestration pattern for this item.
- **Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)** — completed; sibling that added Scout fire sound + advance cue (per-entity two-phase tell with a gap — the gap this item's operator feedback flags for removal).
- **Remove the gap between Scout advance cue and shot (AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU)** — created from this intake (discovered-from), operator-requested follow-up: apply the same no-gap treatment to Scout.
- **Ensure enemy best practices document include instructions for audio on spawn, shoot and explode (AH-0MTCNZFCD009P5IB)** — open, sibling; overlaps with this item's documentation ACs.
- **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** — completed; created the scene/entity this item extends.
- **Update E4/E5/Boss work items to adhere to core-library best practices (AH-0MTAN51HO007A92H)** — completed; established the `effects.ts` audio pattern and base-class audio ownership.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Double-play risk**: the base `GymFormationScene` plays `playDestructionSound()` in both destruction paths. The Tank must NOT call it in its own explosion path (design doc §7). Assumption: "reuse" (Q3) confirms the shared destruction sound; the once-only guarantee is an AC.
- **No-gap cue timing**: the mechanical whine must still satisfy the GDD ≥ 500 ms advance-lead requirement while flowing into the thump with no dead gap. Assumption: whine duration itself provides the lead (cue starts ≥ 500 ms before the shot lands); implementer to verify exact timing in tests (cue → thump ordering, minimal gap).
- **Scene-level orchestration**: bursts are collected scene-level (`collectBullets`); the Swarm-style new-bullet detection in `GymTank.update()` is the established pattern. Assumption: one cue+thump pair per burst is acceptable even if two tanks fire in nearly the same frame (operator: "one", not per-entity).
- **Dead-code `playTankDestructionSound()`**: defined but unused; the implementer either leaves it untouched or removes it — it must NOT be repurposed as the fire sound (operator: "new", Q2 round 2).
- **Testability**: existing enemy tests do not exercise audio; new tests spy/mock `src/audio/effects` to assert call counts/ordering in headless runs.
- **Scope creep**: no other enemy audio work is implied (Diver is a separate pre-existing open item AH-0MTCO1LGD0082SVG; the Scout gap is tracked in AH-0MTF1I1S8003P0GU). Record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (round 1)**: Fire sound character — single heavy low "cannon thump" per burst (one sound for the 10-shot radial burst, scene-level, Swarm-style) or a short zap per GDD §7.3 catalog wording? — **Answer (producer): "1. heavy thump (update the GDD to allow this kind of decision without questioning the producer)"** — heavy cannon thump; GDD must record that audio-character decisions are per-enemy at implementation. # Intake Brief: Enemy Best Practices — Audio Instructions

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, consolidated "Audio Best Practices" section to `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` covering spawn, shoot (fire), and explode (destruction) sounds — including when to call each function, scope rules (entity vs scene level), and per-enemy audio decisions.

---

## Problem Statement

The enemy best practices document (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) currently scatters audio-related guidance across a few checklist items and a table. There is no clear, consolidated set of instructions telling developers and AI agents **when to play audio, which function to call, and at what scope** for spawn, shoot, and explode events. This makes it easy to forget audio or wire it incorrectly when creating new enemy gym scenes.

## Users

- **AI agents and developers** creating new enemy gym scenes (e.g., E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, Boss)
- **Code reviewers** verifying that audio is correctly implemented in new scenes

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new `## Audio Best Practices` section exists in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, clearly organized by event type (spawn, shoot, explode/destruction).
2. The spawn section specifies: which function to call (`playSpawnSound()`), when (during entity creation in the spawn loop), and scope (base class owns this — §3.1 checklist item 5 confirms base handles it).
3. The shoot section specifies: which functions to call per enemy type (e.g., `playScoutAdvanceCue()` + `playScoutFireSound()` for Scout, `playTankAdvanceCue()` + `playTankFireSound()` for Tank, `playSwarmBurstSound()` for Swarm), when to call each (advance cue timing, fire sound timing), scope rules (entity-level vs scene-level), and the no-gap pattern for Tank.
4. The explode/destruction section specifies: which function to call (`playDestructionSound()`), when (during entity destruction), and the critical ownership rule (base class owns destruction sound — entities must NOT call `playDestructionSound()` to avoid double-playing).
5. The section references `src/audio/effects.ts` as the source of all audio functions and links to GDD §7.3 for the audio event catalog.

## Constraints

4. **Advance audio cue** (removed per operator feedback): Originally requested a ≥ 500 ms warning cue before firing (mirroring Phaser). 5. **Headless test safety**: All new audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless/test environments (return early if `getAudioContext()` is null).

# Swarm enemies are too small

## Problem statement

Swarm enemies (E5, GDD §4.1) render as 10 px-wide neon-blue diamonds — too small to read clearly during the dense, fast cluster movement that defines the E5 Swarm, the highest-threat regular enemy by positional density. The fix grows them to 15 px spans (a 50% increase).

- **Player / developer playtesting** — wants swarm clusters that are readable during fast, dense movement; currently too small to track.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need the reference Swarm implementation (`src/entities/Swarm.ts`) sized per the visual intent.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want Swarm enemies to render larger (diamond spans 15 px instead of ~10 px) so the E5 cluster is clearly visible in the gym scene.
- As a **developer**, I want the size change to stay a single-constant tweak (no behaviour changes) so cluster movement, pass-through, and burst shooting are untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Size 15 px:** Swarm diamonds render at 15 px spans (`SWARM_SIZE` 10 → 15 in `src/entities/Swarm.ts`).
- [ ] **AC2 — Visual style preserved:** The enlarged diamond keeps the GDD §4.1 blue `#0066ff` body (2 px stroke, 0.35 fill) applied after the graphics `clear()` (the existing browser-render regression guard still passes).
- [ ] **AC3 — Explosion scales:** The destruction animation rings/radius scale with the new size — they derive from `SWARM_SIZE` — verified via the gym Explode control or a test.
- [ ] **AC4 — Behaviour unchanged:** Formation offsets, cluster drift, swarm pass-through, and coordinated bursts behave as before; spacing/cluster logic unchanged (at 15 px members do not overlap — 16.8 px intra-cluster gap > 15 px span).
- [ ] **AC5 — Size regression test:** `src/entities/Swarm.test.ts` gains/extends a geometry assertion pinning the 15 px diamond extent, so a future size regression is caught; existing entity and gym suites pass.

- [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Phaser v4 + TypeScript; prefer a minimal change in `src/entities/Swarm.ts` (`SWARM_SIZE`) so bullets, bursts, audio cues, and pass-through are untouched.
- Swarms pass freely through one another by design (GDD §2.6).
- Out of scope: `SWARM_BULLET_SIZE`, bullet speed, audio, and other enemy types (scope-creep would be new work items).

## Existing state

# Scout has no audio (AH-0MTCO1LDA008RA19)

**Headline:** The E1 Scout enemy is silent on its player-facing firing event — no fire sound when it shoots an aimed shot, and no advance audio cue before it fires. Add a Scout-specific fire sound (a sharp laser-like blip) and a firing advance audio cue (≥ 500 ms lead) following the established procedural-audio pattern; destruction audio reuses the shared `playDestructionSound()` already played by the base scene.

## Problem statement

The E1 Scout entity (`src/entities/Scout.ts`) plays no audio on its firing event: `tryFireAimedBullet()` creates bullets silently, with no fire sound and no pre-fire warning. Destruction audio is already covered by the base class `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()` (shared `playDestructionSound()`, per `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §7), so the gap is on the firing side. The Scout breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be announced by an advance cue with ≥ 500 ms lead) and is inconsistent with its peers (Phaser plays an advance cue + destruction sound; Swarm has a burst sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a scout fires (danger cue) and a pre-fire warning so aimed shots are telegraphed, per GDD §7.3.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Scout audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) so headless tests stay green and the enemy core-library best practices apply.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a sound when a scout fires its aimed shot so I can react to the projectile.
- As a player, I want an audio cue at least 500 ms before a scout fires so I can anticipate the shot.
- As a developer, I want Scout audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Destruction sound (reuse)** — Destroying a Scout plays the shared `playDestructionSound()` exactly once per destruction. This is currently satisfied by `GymFormationScene.explodeRandom()`; the implementer must ensure the Scout entity does **not** add its own destruction-sound call in `playExplosion()` (no double-play), and a test locks in the once-only behaviour.
- **Scout fire sound** — A new Scout-specific fire sound exists in `src/audio/effects.ts` (e.g. `playScoutFireSound()` — a sharp laser-like blip distinct from the destruction burst and the Swarm buzz), played exactly **once** per aimed shot fired (per-entity, at the point of firing — Scout shots are independent, not coordinated volleys).
- **Advance audio cue** — The Scout plays a firing advance audio cue ≥ 500 ms before each aimed shot (per-entity tell phase, mirroring the Phaser pattern), verified for ordering relative to the fire sound (cue precedes shot).
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the §3.2 scene table row for `GymScout` currently lists audio as "none").
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays spawn/destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — the implementer must reconcile entity-level vs scene-level audio to avoid double-play.
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Scout.ts` — `tryFireAimedBullet()` fires silently; no audio imports, no tell/advance-cue state machine. Fire interval `SCOUT_FIRE_INTERVAL = 1200` ms; shots are independent per entity.
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — has `playSpawnSound`, `playDestructionSound`, `playTankDestructionSound`, power-up/weapon cues, `playSwarmBurstSound`, `playSwarmAdvanceCue`; **no Scout-specific fire sound exists**.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — base class plays `playSpawnSound()` at spawn (line 148) and `playDestructionSound()` in `explodeRandom()` (line 198) for all enemy gyms (design doc §6/§7 says these are base-class-owned).
- `src/entities/Phaser.ts` (reference) — two-phase tell state machine (`_isTelling`/`_tellStartTime`): first call after the fire interval starts the tell (plays `_playAdvanceCue()`, a 660→880 Hz rising sine over `PHASER_ADVANCE_CUE_DURATION = 600` ms) and returns no bullets; the next call after the tell duration fires and returns bullets.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3.2 — scene table lists `GymScout` audio as "none".
- `src/entities/Scout.test.ts` — existing "fires an aimed bullet only when shoot mode is enabled and the interval has elapsed" test expects a bullet on the first eligible call; this test **will need updating** once a tell phase is introduced (first eligible call starts the tell and returns null).

## Desired change

**Headline:** The E2 Diver enemy is silent on its player-facing events: its spread bursts (3–5 projectiles, fired during a dive) produce no fire sound, and — per producer decision — its destruction should use a distinct Diver-specific sound rather than the shared generic burst. Add a Diver-specific fire sound played once per spread burst (procedural Web Audio, safe no-op without an AudioContext) and a distinct Diver destruction sound, wired through a minimal optional seam in the base `GymFormationScene` so it plays exactly once per destruction (no double-play). No firing advance cue is added (producer decision).

## Problem statement

The E2 Diver entity (`src/entities/Diver.ts`) plays no audio on its firing event: `tryFireSpreadBurst()` spawns 3–5 projectiles silently. Its destruction currently relies on the shared `playDestructionSound()` given to all enemies by `GymFormationScene`, but the producer wants a distinct Diver-specific destruction sound. The Diver breaks the GDD §7.3 audio-feedback design (enemy fire should be audible) and is inconsistent with its peers (Scout plays a fire sound, Tank plays a cue+thump, Swarm has a burst sound).

## Users

- **Players** — need audible feedback when a diver fires its spread burst (danger cue) and a distinct destruction sound so a diver explosion is distinguishable from Scout/Tank/Swarm explosions.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need Diver audio to follow the established procedural-audio pattern (`src/audio/effects.ts`) and the enemy core-library best practices so the shared base scene is not broken and headless tests stay green.

### Example user stories

- As a player, I want to hear a distinct sound when a diver fires its spread burst so I can react to the projectiles.
- As a player, I want a diver's destruction to sound different from other enemies so I can tell what kind of enemy I just destroyed.
- As a developer, I want Diver audio implemented via the existing `effects.ts` helpers and a minimal, backward-compatible seam in the base scene so it degrades to a safe no-op in headless tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Diver fire sound** — A new `playDiverFireSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts` (distinct from the Scout blip, the Swarm buzz, and the Tank thump — e.g. a short low/nasal crack appropriate to the dive), played exactly **once per spread burst** (not once per projectile; the 3–5 bullet burst shares one sound).
- **No advance cue** — No firing advance cue (≥ 500 ms tell) is added to the Diver path; the fire sound plays at the moment the burst is fired. A test or explicit no-op documents that no cue helper is wired in.
- **Distinct destruction sound** — A new `playDiverDestructionSound()` exists in `src/audio/effects.ts` (distinct from the shared destruction burst and the Diver fire sound), played exactly **once per diver destruction** with no double-play of the shared `playDestructionSound()`. The Diver entity must NOT call a destruction sound in `playExplosion()`.
- **Wiring seam** — The base `GymFormationScene` gains a minimal optional per-entity hook (e.g. optional `playDestructionAudio?()` on `FormationSceneEntity`, mirroring the existing `setAimTarget?()` precedent) used by the two enemy-destruction call sites (`explodeRandom()` and `_handleCollisions()`); entities without the hook (Scout/Tank/Swarm/Phaser) keep the shared `playDestructionSound()`. Existing base-scene and enemy tests must pass unchanged.
- **Safe degradation** — All new audio calls are safe no-ops without a working `AudioContext` (headless tests, browsers without Web Audio), preserving the `effects.ts` contract.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (if it lists per-enemy audio), and `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (the §3.2 scene-table row for `GymDiver` currently lists audio as "none"; §6/§7 should note the optional per-entity destruction-sound seam).
- **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes (no CI/CD pipeline tests).

## Constraints

- Procedural Web Audio only — no audio assets (existing `effects.ts` pattern).
- Follow enemy core-library best practices (`docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`); the base `GymFormationScene` already plays destruction sounds for all enemy gyms — the implementer must avoid double-play when the Diver switches to a distinct sound.
- The base-scene seam must be backward compatible: entities that do not opt in keep current behaviour (shared sound).
- Audio functions must degrade to safe no-ops in headless environments.
- Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Diver.ts` — `tryFireSpreadBurst()` fires 3–5 projectiles silently (`DIVER_BURST_COUNT = 4`, `DIVER_FIRE_INTERVAL = 1000` ms, bursts fire during the dive); no audio imports, no sound calls. `playExplosion()` plays only VFX.

- **Diver entity**: call `playDiverFireSound()` exactly once per spread burst inside `tryFireSpreadBurst()` (when a burst is actually produced). - `src/entities/Diver.test.ts` — add fire-sound-once-per-burst test and destruction-sound-once/no-double-play test (spy/mock the `effects` module).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymDiver.test.ts` — scene-level regression: audio no-op degradation; destruction hook used exactly once with no double-play.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts` — regression: entities without the hook still play the shared sound once (if needed).

Assumption: per-entity call site is acceptable; if the producer preferred scene-level, that is a small adjustment.
